summary: AstroHealth AI is an AI-powered, offline-capable health monitoring and clinical decision-support platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It monitors vital health indicators in real time, detects potential medical anomalies, and visualizes health conditions through an interactive Digital Twin. The platform also provides AI-assisted medical consultations using a RAG system based on NASA Human Research Program resources, generates countermeasure recommendations, and offers preloaded emergency protocols that remain accessible without an internet connection. Additionally, it ensures secure medical data synchronization with Earth using HMAC-SHA256. By addressing communication delays and the limited availability of immediate medical assistance during deep-space missions, AstroHealth AI aims to improve astronauts' health monitoring, medical response, and autonomy, ultimately contributing to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.
details: AstroHealth AI is an AI-powered, offline-capable health monitoring and clinical decision-support platform developed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions, particularly missions to the Moon and Mars, where communication delays with Earth can reach up to 20 minutes each way. The platform continuously monitors vital health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen levels, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep quality, cognitive fatigue, and radiation exposure. It analyzes incoming telemetry data against personalized health baselines and uses a 3-of-5 rolling-window detection mechanism to identify potential health anomalies while reducing false alerts. An interactive 2D Digital Twin visualizes health risks across six anatomical systems, allowing users to identify affected regions and understand their health status. The platform also features an AI-powered medical assistant based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which retrieves relevant knowledge from NASA Human Research Program resources to provide context-based medical guidance and predefined countermeasure recommendations. To ensure medical support remains accessible during communication failures, AstroHealth AI includes an offline AI fallback engine and a Trauma Override feature that provides instantly accessible emergency checklists with voice assistance. Additionally, it generates secure medical reports for synchronization with Earth and uses HMAC-SHA256 to verify data integrity and detect unauthorized modifications. We developed the frontend using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, while the backend uses Python, FastAPI, SQLite, and SQLAlchemy. Other technologies include WebSockets for real-time communication, Google Gemini for online AI processing, NumPy for similarity calculations, and the Web Speech API for voice assistance. The creativity of our project lies in integrating real-time monitoring, an interactive Digital Twin, knowledge-grounded AI, offline emergency response, and secure communication into one unified platform rather than treating them as separate solutions. Throughout development, we considered communication delays, limited connectivity, astronaut safety, medical information reliability, false alerts, data privacy, security, and usability during stressful situations. AstroHealth AI aims to reduce dependence on immediate ground-based medical assistance, improve early detection of potential health risks, strengthen medical autonomy, and contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration. The current implementation is a functional prototype that uses synthetic demonstration data and is not a certified medical device.
